recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Restoring the exact 2015 sentence would conflict with later Published document-page decisions; any future change should be handled as a new FHIR-I clarification if implementers find the current attestation/update-policy language insufficient.
issue_request: FHIR-7388 was a Published FHIR-core documents issue, resolved Persuasive with Modification, asking to soften the DSTU1 statement that document content and presentation could not change so that only substantial changes that alter clinical meaning were prohibited.
initial_application: Git commit 680c9f5b1460104c5dc910df5b59d0d2a61fc8f7, matching the Jira comment for svn revision 6448, applied the approved qualifier to source/documents.html by saying directly referenced content and document presentation cannot change substantially if that changes clinical meaning.
additional_context: Later Published FHIR-I decisions rewrote the same FHIR Documents guidance. FHIR-36636 removed the old immutable-document paragraph and replaced it with attestation-risk and update-policy guidance. FHIR-38927 and FHIR-38930 further refined the introduction by removing overbroad frozen/immutability terminology. Current source/documents.html remains an active top-level page linked from source/documentation.html.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. The current source no longer contains the obsolete unsoftened cannot-change sentence or the old immutable-document paragraph, and the stylesheet section still states that stylesheets SHALL NOT alter presentation in a way that changes clinical meaning.
